rules: Commands affecting one desktop must run sequentially, including screenshots taken after actions.
ok reports command execution; assert data.exists, data.conditionMet or an application postcondition separately.
verified is null when verification was not requested; successful input delivery does not prove the expected result.
Selectors are case-insensitive literal/wildcard matches by default. -Regex accepts regular expressions, not wildcard syntax.
TimeoutMs bounds retries; an individual UI Automation provider call may exceed it.
Use -Flag=value for values starting with a dash. Negative numeric values also work as separate tokens.

GuiNavigation is the default: bounded press-key navigation and audited focused literal input use the GUI. Explicit VisibleControls stays strict and forbids press-key. Application hotkeys/Shortcut clearing require authorized AllowShortcuts; clipboard is unsupported.
Commands use a bounded desktop mutex. DesktopBusy means not dispatched; outcome unknown requires observing the postcondition before retry.
Invalid bounds are returned as null with boundsStatus/propertyErrors; do not infer missing UIA support from missing geometry.

UIA bounds, screenshots and mouse points use physical screen pixels in every transport. Desktop commands temporarily set thread DPI awareness and restore it afterwards. Screenshot region.x/y is the image origin; never copy coordinates from a resized preview.

help.notes: Read command guidance without a desktop session or state mutation. Topics combines several commands with one copy of shared rules; avoid separate process starts for each topic.

state.notes: Clear resets CLI context, not application state.

start.notes: FilePath/Path and positional launch target are also accepted. KillExisting is destructive and must only be used for disposable test-owned apps. Check data.windowFound. A file-association launch does not exercise an application's Open UI. Only executable launches are accepted. RequireNewProcess waits briefly for a closing prior instance, rejects a still-running app, and returns ownedProcessId for scoped cleanup.

windows.notes: With ProcessId, includes modal Window descendants exposed beneath the owner in UIA; data.windows includes isModal. A nonempty windows result is eligible exploration evidence for window/title state. File creation/content need their own receipts. Close owned dialogs before parent windows.

observe.notes: Compact returns actionable flat elements, focusedElement, live bounds, patterns and candidate selectors; check uniqueness before acting. Full (CLI default) preserves the nested tree. FocusedWindow inspects the owned foreground window. Name/SelectorJson/PathJson can anchor a subtree. Depth 0..20, MaxElements 1..2000. limitReached means the node budget was exhausted; depthBoundaryReached means descendants at the depth boundary were not inspected (not proof that they exist). A missing control in a bounded tree is not proof of UIA absence. Before coordinate fallback, scope deeper discovery to an observed container or search a short label fragment with select -Name '*fragment*' -TimeoutMs 0. Opaque Pane roles can change as providers initialize.

select.notes: Queries elements; it does not select a dropdown item. data.count=0 is a valid query result. Open a dropdown before looking for its items. Use SelectorJson with a Name array for alternative labels in one query; TimeoutMs 0 is useful for discovery. Scope FocusedWindow searches the owned foreground dialog without relying on IsModal. Add role/class constraints only to disambiguate, especially for opaque Pane controls.

click.usage: click <selector options> [-RequireUnique true] [-Method Auto|Mouse|Invoke] [-RelativeX 0.5 -RelativeY 0.5] [-Center true] [-Button Left|Right] [-Focus false] [-ElementFocus false] [-OffsetX 0] [-OffsetY 0] [-VerifyDisappeared]
click.notes: Use default Auto, which tries supported UIA patterns then a visible mouse click. RequireUnique defaults true: multiple visible enabled matches fail before input with error.candidates. Add an observed ID, role, class or parent scope; do not blindly choose the first label. RequireUnique false explicitly restores legacy first-match behavior. Explicit Invoke is checked before changing focus and requires InvokePattern. Scope FocusedWindow targets controls in the owned foreground dialog. Mouse uses live geometry. RelativeX/Y select a point within live bounds (fractions 0..1, both required) and force mouse input; do not combine with offsets/Center/Invoke. For menus already open, Focus false and ElementFocus false avoid changing focus before the click. Observe the postcondition before retrying.

click-coordinate.notes: Fallback only; retain a screenshot and explain the missing selector route.

type.usage: type -Text 'literal text' [<selector options>] [-TargetMode Writable|Focused] [-ExpectedFocusJson <identity selector> -FocusTimeoutMs 2000] [-FallbackReason <reason> -FallbackEvidence <reference>] [-FocusMethod Auto|UIA|Mouse] [-PreDelete] [-ClearMethod Selection|Shortcut] [-Verify] [-VerifyMode Exact|Contains|NormalizedExact|NormalizedContains] [-VerifyTimeoutMs 3000] [-MaxAttempts 0] [-TypeByCharacter] [-Focus]
type.notes: Literal Unicode keyboard input, never clipboard. Writable mode is default and checks UIA writability/focus; selector Auto focus falls back to a visible click. Multiline literals require a writable Document target, not a nested single-line Edit. Focused mode is an explicit audited fallback for an observed opaque editor: existing focus only, no target selector/refocus/PreDelete/newlines/tabs, and explicit read-only still fails. ExpectedFocusJson optionally waits for observed focus identity and owned foreground readiness without clicking/refocusing or losing an existing selection; FocusTimeoutMs is 0..10000. It is a guard, not a focus action. Both modes check the actual foreground application or owned dialog. Verify polls current readback without resending or committing. For commit-on-exit controls, type once without Verify, commit through an observed control or permitted press-key Enter, then read/assert. Normalized modes reconcile line endings. TimeoutMs is lookup time; VerifyTimeoutMs is readback time. For replacement prefer writable PreDelete plus Verify; PreDelete uses TextPattern selection and Backspace. Do not click an already selected filename just to wait for focus. Shortcut clearing requires authorization.

press-key.notes: GuiNavigation/AllowShortcuts only. Sends bounded navigation to confirmed focus in the working application or its owned dialog and returns focus before/after. Count is 1..20; Enter/Escape must be single actions followed by an observation. No application hotkeys, function keys, clipboard, key expressions, or implicit refocus. Required menu/button routes still apply. Dispatch does not verify the application postcondition.

hotkey.notes: Disabled by default, including Enter confirmations. One chord only, no grouped sequences or clipboard shortcuts. Requires user/testcase permission.

drag.notes: Click/hold, move, and drop using the left mouse button. Each endpoint can be a selector (including nested paths) or coordinates. Resolves both visible/enabled controls before pressing. Fractions choose a point inside current element bounds; defaults are centers. Movement is smooth by default; DurationMs is 50..10000. Always releases the button on failure. released/dragged mean input delivery; assert the actual drop result separately. Coordinate endpoints need observed fallback evidence.

wait-element.notes: Assert data.exists, not just ok. Use the selector's TimeoutMs. Window queries in Scope FocusedWindow include the owned foreground dialog itself, not just its descendants. Ordinary window queries include the working window and other process windows. FocusedWindow waits refresh the scope between failed probes. A launched window does not prove the application's next control is ready.

wait-file.notes: Assert data.conditionMet. StableMs requires unchanged length AND last-write time. Directories are not files. Stability alone does not prove file validity or content. Use unique execution paths to avoid stale-file passes.

read.notes: Returns data.text and data.textSource (ValuePattern, TextPattern, or Name fallback). Content assertions require a text pattern; an element name proves only its label. After reopening, read the document control and assert every required content fragment. Use read, not empty typing, to observe text.

read-pdf.notes: Read-only text extraction; returns data.path, data.text, and data.reader. Auto tries the built-in simple PDF reader, then optional installed Python+pypdf if PythonPath or POTATO_PDF_PYTHON is configured. The shipped helper avoids inline-code quoting and never creates expected outputs. Builtin has no dependencies but rejects object/xref streams and other unsupported layouts. Neither reader performs OCR; missing/empty text fails. No desktop or session-state mutation.

screenshot.notes: Returns physical-pixel imageWidth/imageHeight, region and coordinateSpace. Inspect the actual image before choosing a fallback point; a screenshot path alone is not visual inspection. Add region.x/y to image pixel coordinates. Capture alone is not an assertion, and hardcoded coordinates still depend on application layout.

close-window.notes: With no selector, targets only the working window. A ProcessId query includes nested modal windows and closes them before the parent. An explicit selector miss never closes another working window. data.closed counts accepted close requests; inspect remaining windows for cleanup verification.

report.notes: Records a report event; it does not validate that the status is justified.

globalOptions.InteractionPolicy: GuiNavigation (default), VisibleControls (strict), or explicitly authorized AllowShortcuts
globalOptions.FallbackReason: Required explanation for focused opaque typing, press-key, and authorized shortcuts
globalOptions.FallbackEvidence: Required observation/screenshot reference for focused opaque typing, press-key, and authorized shortcuts
